Frac_large_nucleus gave Spearman rho=-1.00 (e9) because the signal was already saturated at 0.1 uM (z=+86.2 in e7) and then slightly lower at higher doses, not because of a true inverse response. ## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean validation of identity (2.4%) and integrity (2.3% 530 bp) with no contamination or misidentification.

## Unblinding

Compound: **AZ841** (PubChem CID [12001839](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/12001839))

Identity check: from the BBBC021 structure (the name is not in PubChem)

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Aurora kinase inhibitors**.

## Reflection

The Aurora call was correct because the core phenotype was extreme and consistent: frac_large_nucleus z=+60.3 to +86.2 at 0.1-1 uM (e3, e7) with enlarged irregular nuclei, low form-factor and solidity, plus very high DNA content at 30 uM (nuc_dna_integrated z=+41.9 in e2). Visual description of similar density with enlarged irregular nuclei (e4) and atlas match of 6/10 Aurora kinase inhibitors (e5) correctly outweighed the 4/10 microtubule-destabilizer neighbors.

What misled was the dose-response interpretation from only 4 wells. Frac_large_nucleus gave Spearman rho=-1.00 (e9) because the signal was already saturated at 0.1 uM (z=+86.2 in e7) and then slightly lower at higher doses, not because of a true inverse response. Tubulin, mitotic-like fraction and DNA trends (e10-e12, rho=+0.80, p=0.2) were non-significant with n=4 and could not formally exclude microtubule effects, yet I upgraded Aurora to 0.84 on that basis; high-dose rounding and solidity (cell_roundness z=+37.6 in e2) was also left as unexplained secondary toxicity.

Acquisition choices helped by sampling low, mid and high doses (e2, e3, e7, e8), but missing the lowest 0.01 uM dose and replicates left no EC50 onset, and post-unblinding literature work was weak: AZ841 had no curated mechanism (e15) and searches for 'AZ841 Aurora' (e16) and polyploidy-cytokinesis linkage (e17, 0 hits) did not validate the mechanism. Literature in this run supports Aurora inhibitors as an established investigational class (PMID 22242557, PMID 24965505) with reported Aurora-inhibition vulnerability contexts (PMID 28089889).

What was right:
- Prioritized massive polyploidy signal: frac_large_nucleus z=+60 to +86 and nuc_area z=+27.1 at 0.1-1 uM (e3, e7) over high-dose rounding.
- Used intact microtubule inference and visual check (e4) plus atlas 6/10 Aurora (e5) to favor Aurora over microtubule destabilizers and Eg5.
- Recognized high DNA content (e2, e12) with irregular low solidity/form-factor nuclei as failed cytokinesis/endoreduplication rather than simple mitotic arrest.

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-interpreted e9 rho=-1.00 as saturating dose-response when it reflected ceiling effect already maximal at 0.1 uM.
- Treated e10-e12 trends as discriminatory despite p=0.2 with only 4 wells, leaving tubulin-flat and no-arrest claims underpowered.
- Kept microtubule destabilizers at 0.08 too long from atlas 4/10 similarity and did not acquire lowest dose or replicate to define onset and rule out secondary high-dose toxicity seen in e2.

Proposed next experiment: Phospho-histone H3 Ser10 immunofluorescence dose-response with Aurora A/B target engagement plus live-cell imaging for failed cytokinesis and endoreduplication, run alongside a demecolcine microtubule-destabilizer control to separate polyploidy from tubulin loss.

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [22242557](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22242557/): Danusertib, an aurora kinase inhibitor. *Expert Opin Investig Drugs* (2012) — Danusertib is a described example of an Aurora kinase inhibitor.
- PMID [24965505](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24965505/): Aurora kinase inhibitor patents and agents in clinical testing: an update (2011 - 2013). *Expert Opin Ther Pat* (2014) — Aurora kinase inhibitors have been extensively patented and evaluated as investigational agents.
- PMID [28089889](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28089889/): MYC Drives Progression of Small Cell Lung Cancer to a Variant Neuroendocrine Subtype with Vulnerability to Aurora Kinase Inhibition. *Cancer Cell* (2017) — Vulnerability to Aurora kinase inhibition has been reported in a variant neuroendocrine subtype of small cell lung cancer.
